title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 201: Harnessing Nature's Glow
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 201 (LEVEL B1 • BAND 5.0)

Harnessing Nature's Glow: The Science of Living Light

Paragraph 1. Public lighting accounts for nearly twenty percent of municipal electricity costs worldwide. To cut carbon emissions, biologists and urban planners are exploring bioluminescence—cold light produced naturally by fireflies, deep-sea fish, and glowing fungi without an electric grid. Whereas traditional bulbs convert under ten percent of electricity into light, bioluminescent reactions reach nearly ninety-eight percent optical efficiency. Biochemist Dr. Claire Moreau notes that nature solved sustainable lighting millions of years ago; our task is building living systems stable enough to last months.

Paragraph 2. Early trials inserting bacterial genes into ornamental plants produced dim results and stunted plant growth. Geneticists therefore turned to glowing fungi such as Neonothopanus nambi. Unlike bacteria needing chemical additives, fungal light shares pathways with caffeic acid, a natural substance present in all land plants, boosting autonomous green glow a thousand-fold without harming the plant.

Paragraph 3. Biophysicist Dr. Kenneth Vance tested glowing microalgae across sixty underground transit stations in Brussels. His team mounted vertical glass columns filled with photosynthetic algae along pedestrian corridors. Daytime sunlight directed via optical fibres helped algae store energy; at night, mechanical pumps circulated air bubbles to trigger an ethereal blue glow while sensors logged brightness and commuter feedback.

Paragraph 4. Sociologist Dr. Aris Thorne explains that city dwellers are accustomed to harsh LED glare, so many commuters initially felt uneasy around dim biological panels. Yet after several weeks, public opinion turned strongly positive, with residents reporting lower evening stress and a calming emotional connection.

Paragraph 5. Ecological toxicologist Dr. Haruki Sato urges caution: blue-green light overlaps with signals used by migrating birds and insects, risking disruption to avian navigation and bat foraging. He insists on strict environmental assessments first. Looking ahead, Dr. Moreau sees living lights guiding footpaths and parks rather than replacing bright highway grids.

groups.title: Questions 1–5
groups.instructions: Complete the notes. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage.
groups.template:

  • Fungal light works with caffeic 2. {{q2}} found naturally in plants.

groups.title: Questions 6–10
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

q6.text: Why do planners consider bioluminescence superior to incandescent bulbs?
options: A. It requires brighter electric grids.
B. It produces stronger heat.
C. It wastes almost no energy as heat.
D. It only works inside highways.

steps: Đoạn 1: Hiệu suất ánh sáng gần 98%, hầu như không tỏa nhiệt → C.

q7.text: What problem occurred in early bacterial trials on plants?
options: A. The plants grew poorly and glowed dimly.
B. The plants glowed too brightly for cameras.
C. The plants killed local insects.
D. The bacteria needed glass columns.

steps: Đoạn 2: Cây phát sáng yếu và bị còi cọc → A.

q8.text: How did commuters in Brussels first react to bioluminescent panels?
options: A. They immediately demanded them on highways.
B. They ignored the panels completely.
C. They reported lower stress on day one.
D. They felt uneasy because the light seemed dim.

steps: Đoạn 4: Ban đầu thấy lo ngại vì ánh sáng dịu hơn đèn LED → D.

q9.text: What does Dr. Haruki Sato insist must happen before commercial rollout?
options: A. Replacing all LEDs in Europe.
B. Conducting thorough environmental impact reviews.
C. Painting park trees blue.
D. Removing bats from city parks.

steps: Đoạn 5: Đánh giá tác động môi trường nghiêm ngặt trước khi triển khai → B.

q10.text: How does Dr. Claire Moreau envision using living lights in cities?
options: A. Guiding walkways alongside traditional highway lighting.
B. Eliminating all conventional electricity permanently.
C. Lighting only underground train tunnels.
D. Replacing indoor house lamps.

steps: Đoạn 5: Dùng dẫn đường lối đi, công viên kết hợp đèn lưới cho cao tốc → A.
